items.title: The symbol of a discrete valuation ring equals the usual tame symbol
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: For a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and nonzero x, y in K, the lemma identifies the symbol d_A(x, y) with (-1)^{ord_A(x) ord_A(y)} x^{ord_A(y)} / y^{ord_A(x)} modulo the maximal ideal (statement lines 17623-17634). The proof first uses multiplicativity of the symbol to reduce to x, y in A, writes x = t^a u and y = t^b v with t a uniformizer and u, v units, sets l = a + b, observes that t^{l-1}, ..., t^b is an admissible sequence in (x)/(xy) and t^{l-1}, ..., t^a is an admissible sequence in (y)/(xy), and invokes the characterisation of the symbol by a single comparison of two such symbols to obtain the equation defining d_A(x, y) with the sign (-1)^{ab} (proof lines 17637-17650). The last step evaluates the two symbols through the admissible relations to get d_A(x, y) = (-1)^{ab} u^a / v^b mod m_A (proof lines 17651-17654). Choosing the two admissible sequences in the quotients correctly and reducing the comparison to the unit parts is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
